_about: 777-200 and -200ER, from Boeing D6-58329 Rev E 2.2.1 (page index 19): side, plan and front views on one sheet, drawn 5.7% larger than D6-58329-2's 777F sheet (2.2.3). Pixels of layers.py rasters at scale 20, line centres. The B77L's (777F's) points, moved onto this sheet (plug.py with no plugs: --scale 1.057) and snapped; the wing's tip re-placed where this sheet ends it (the 777-200's plain tip, 60.93 m, where the 777F's raked tip begins). The side view draws the cabin windows as closed outlines in blue strokes (side_all.png: fills and strokes together); those behind the wing's lines (windowsAlso) are placed at the drawing's own pitch, from where they're drawn cut by the wing's lines to door 3. Door 3 is drawn behind the flaps, its top and aft corner showing: placed by them (36.45 m to its middle; 2.7.1 prints 36.33 m). The nacelle is the one the sheet draws (a GE90's shape, its inlet 20.42 m from the nose as printed for the GE90 within 0.6%). The cockpit panes are the B77L's (the same nose), moved as its points are. No wingtip device.

sources.title: Boeing, 777-200/-200ER/-300 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (D6-58329 Rev E, December 2024), 2.2.1 General Dimensions: Model 777-200; 2.7.1 Main Entry Door Locations
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off 2.2.1's side, plan and front views (tools/trace/b772/), starting from the 777F's points (tools/trace/b77l/: the same fuselage, fin, tailplane and inboard wing) moved onto this sheet and snapped; the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The plain wingtip (60.93 m) is this sheet's, ending where the 777F's raked tip begins. The sheet draws the cabin windows; those behind the wing's lines are placed at its own pitch. Doors 1, 2 and 4 are drawn 0.02-0.13 m from 2.7.1's 6.75, 17.07 and 49.54 m; door 3, drawn behind the flaps, is placed by its visible corners (36.45 m against 36.33 m). The nacelle is the one the sheet draws, a GE90-94B's shape: its inlet 20.29 m from the nose against 20.42 m printed for the GE90 (PW4074 20.22 m, Trent 875 20.13 m); 777-200ERs with Trent or PW4000 engines have shorter, slimmer nacelles, not drawn. Width +2.0% and tailplane +1.5% by line centres, as on the 777F's and 777-300ER's sheets; span -0.8%.
